Szczercow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kozłówki, Poland

Not demolished. Szczerców's Jewish community, present from 1790 and initially subordinate to the kehilla in nearby Łask, grew to 35 percent of the town by 1897; many fled to Zelow or Bełchatów at the start of WWII, and those who remained were deported to Bełchatów in 1942. This cemetery — locally known as Jung Mountain — was seriously damaged during the war, and a sand mine was established there afterward, the same fate that befell the cemetery at Zelow, elsewhere in this collection. A dozen or so damaged matzevot survive today, all displaced from their original positions, but the site continues to suffer ongoing vandalism and illegal sand extraction, and human bones periodically surface from the sandy, poorly maintained ground.
